natural_body: Deep discounts spike signups +31% but risk renewal. Use tactically with guardrails.

first.rationale: Two of the three current problems are onboarding completion (-4%) and activation (-6%), which are exactly the funnel stages memory_86 and memory_31 speak to, so the inherited evidence is closest in kind to the present deficit. I want the archived records for those two because both are consolidated summaries whose headline metrics are proxies: memory_86 reports completion and time-to-value, memory_31 reports first-week activation, and neither states whether the lift persisted into renewal or qualified revenue, which is the actual objective. The verification should reveal the original cohort (SMB self-serve vs. all accounts), the measurement window, and whether any downstream revenue metric was tracked. Promotional pricing is the tempting response to the competitor's entry pricing, but memory_73 explicitly pairs a +31% signup spike with renewal risk, and a discount war against a lower-cost entrant tends to import price-sensitive accounts that depress long-term qualified revenue, so it fails the primary objective even though it would move the most visible near-term number. Referral incentive (memory_57) targets established customers and does not address the activation or onboarding decline; enterprise sales-assist (memory_44) is credible but addresses a segment that is not where the current bleed is. The main risk I am carrying into simplify_onboarding is that shortening or stripping steps can remove the qualification and setup work that makes an account durable, converting a completion-rate win into weaker downstream cohorts; the earlier records may simply not have measured long enough to see that. So I will run it as a standard experiment with a holdout, but instrument renewal-relevant and qualified-revenue metrics rather than declaring success on completion rate, and I will treat the inherited claims as directionally useful rather than settled until the archive confirms the cohort and horizon match today's conditions. If verification shows memory_86 was measured only over a short window or on a non-comparable cohort, I would downgrade to a small guarded test.
